lines.text: Ten goats can eat a whole field of grass in twenty days.
lines.caption: Ten goats can eat a whole field of grass in twenty days.

lines.text: Add just five more goats, and they finish in ten days. <short pause> Half the time!
lines.caption: Add just five more goats, and they finish in ten days. Half the time!

lines.text: So how do five more goats save ten whole days? Hi, I'm Vantee. Let's find out together.
lines.caption: So how do five more goats save ten whole days? Hi, I'm Vantee. Let's find out together.

lines.text: Here's the question. A field starts with some grass, and new grass grows at a steady rate.
lines.caption: Here's the question. A field starts with some grass, and new grass grows at a steady rate.

lines.text: Ten goats can eat all the grass in twenty days. Fifteen goats can eat it all in ten days.
lines.caption: Ten goats can eat all the grass in twenty days. Fifteen goats can eat it all in ten days.

lines.text: All goats eat at the same rate. How many days would twenty-five goats take?
lines.caption: All goats eat at the same rate. How many days would twenty-five goats take?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Let's break it down. The grass keeps growing while the goats eat.
lines.caption: Let's break it down. The grass keeps growing while the goats eat.

lines.text: So the goats eat the starting grass, PLUS all the new grass that grows.
lines.caption: So the goats eat the starting grass, PLUS all the new grass that grows.

lines.text: We don't know the starting amount, or how fast it grows. That's two unknowns!
lines.caption: We don't know the starting amount, or how fast it grows. That's two unknowns!

lines.text: Here's a handy unit. One goat-day is the grass that one goat eats in one day.
lines.caption: Here's a handy unit. One goat-day is the grass that one goat eats in one day.

lines.text: Our goal: the number of days for twenty-five goats.
lines.caption: Our goal: the number of days for twenty-five goats.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's count everything in goat-days.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's count everything in goat-days.

lines.text: Ten goats for twenty days eat ten times twenty, which is two hundred goat-days.
lines.caption: Ten goats for twenty days eat ten times twenty, which is two hundred goat-days.

lines.text: Fifteen goats for ten days eat fifteen times ten, which is one hundred fifty goat-days.
lines.caption: Fifteen goats for ten days eat fifteen times ten, which is one hundred fifty goat-days.

lines.text: Both cases start with the same grass. So why did the first goats eat more?
lines.caption: Both cases start with the same grass. So why did the first goats eat more?

lines.text: Because their field had ten more days to grow!
lines.caption: Because their field had ten more days to grow!

lines.text: Those ten extra days grew two hundred minus one hundred fifty, which is fifty goat-days.
lines.caption: Those ten extra days grew two hundred minus one hundred fifty, which is fifty goat-days.

lines.text: Fifty goat-days in ten days is five goat-days each day. Enough to feed five goats!
lines.caption: Fifty goat-days in ten days is five goat-days each day. Enough to feed five goats!

lines.text: In twenty days, the field grows twenty times five, which is one hundred goat-days.
lines.caption: In twenty days, the field grows twenty times five, which is one hundred goat-days.

lines.text: So the starting grass is two hundred minus one hundred, which is one hundred goat-days.
lines.caption: So the starting grass is two hundred minus one hundred, which is one hundred goat-days.

lines.text: Check the fifteen goats: one hundred, plus ten days times five, is one hundred fifty. It matches!
lines.caption: Check the fifteen goats: one hundred, plus ten days times five, is one hundred fifty. It matches!

lines.text: Now let's use twenty-five goats. Each day, they eat twenty-five goat-days.
lines.caption: Now let's use twenty-five goats. Each day, they eat twenty-five goat-days.

lines.text: But five goat-days grow back. So the pile shrinks by twenty-five minus five, which is twenty a day.
lines.caption: But five goat-days grow back. So the pile shrinks by twenty-five minus five, which is twenty a day.

lines.text: One hundred goat-days, at twenty a day, lasts one hundred over twenty, which is five days.
lines.caption: One hundred goat-days, at twenty a day, lasts one hundred over twenty, which is five days.

lines.text: Check: twenty-five times five is one hundred twenty-five. That's one hundred, plus twenty-five more.
lines.caption: Check: twenty-five times five is one hundred twenty-five. That's one hundred, plus twenty-five more.

lines.text: The answer is five days. That's choice B!
lines.caption: The answer is five days. That's choice B!

lines.text: Here's a clever way to picture it. Let's split the goats into two teams.
lines.caption: Here's a clever way to picture it. Let's split the goats into two teams.

lines.text: The helpers eat only the new grass, as fast as it grows. The rest eat the starting pile.
lines.caption: The helpers eat only the new grass, as fast as it grows. The rest eat the starting pile.

lines.text: How many helpers? Let's guess and check. The pile must come out the same in both cases.
lines.caption: How many helpers? Let's guess and check. The pile must come out the same in both cases.

lines.text: No helpers: ten times twenty is two hundred, but fifteen times ten is one hundred fifty.
lines.caption: No helpers: ten times twenty is two hundred, but fifteen times ten is one hundred fifty.

lines.text: Each helper takes twenty off the first pile, but only ten off the second. So the gap shrinks by ten.
lines.caption: Each helper takes twenty off the first pile, but only ten off the second. So the gap shrinks by ten.

lines.text: The gap was fifty, so five helpers close it. Both piles come out at one hundred goat-days!
lines.caption: The gap was fifty, so five helpers close it. Both piles come out at one hundred goat-days!

lines.text: Now twenty-five goats. Five are helpers, and twenty munch the pile.
lines.caption: Now twenty-five goats. Five are helpers, and twenty munch the pile.

lines.text: Twenty goats finish one hundred goat-days in one hundred over twenty: five days. Same answer!
lines.caption: Twenty goats finish one hundred goat-days in one hundred over twenty: five days. Same answer!

lines.text: Pick this way when you like to draw. The helper goats turn a growing field into a pile that stays put.
lines.caption: Pick this way when you like to draw. The helper goats turn a growing field into a pile that stays put.

lines.text: Now the traps. Most of them forget that the grass keeps growing.

lines.text: Six is one hundred fifty over twenty-five, and eight is two hundred over twenty-five.
lines.caption: Six is one hundred fifty over twenty-five, and eight is two hundred over twenty-five.

lines.caption: Fifteen extra days grew sixty sheep-days. That's four sheep-days each day.

lines.text: Thirty days of growth is thirty times four, which is one hundred twenty sheep-days.
lines.caption: Thirty days of growth is thirty times four, which is one hundred twenty sheep-days.

lines.caption: Two hundred forty minus one hundred twenty leaves one hundred twenty to start.

lines.caption: One hundred twenty over twenty is six. The sheep need six days!
